svg.text: HAD / Bedroom 3 after proposed suite relocation
One-sided double-bed access is an explicit tradeoff · no current-house adoption
Gallery / not bedroom
1:50 at A3 · north ↑ · leaf states are separate comparisons
Move only the former en-suite west partition 200 west, from x 9500 to x 9300.
The local east gallery becomes 1070 clear; source west gallery is 1015.
Remove the former en-suite south partition east of x 9300; retain bath north boundary.
Retain the 900 bedroom entrance aperture. Its installed frame/leaf and closure need binding.
A real 1500 ×2000 base plus 90 headboard uses the former en-suite headspace.
East access is 695; west is 25 and is deliberately NOT a usable bedside route.
The south foot field is 1280. Both front windows and the east window have approach points.
Window movement, controls, cleaning and curtains remain actual product/operation duties.
PAX/GRIMO 1000 ×600 ×2012 provides a rail and shelves; no extending drawers are assumed.
Two 500 wardrobe leaves at 90° leave a 600 body comparison between them with the entry closed.
The nominal leaf envelopes include 25 thickness/handle allowance; actual hinge projection differs.
The former lining, branch and gallery panel require explicit IAS removal/reuse dispositions.
Mattress making, two occupants, emergency access, furniture assembly and carrying are not certified.
Connected route comparison
600 mm circular body along every complete axis segment; no diagonal shortcut or human-performance claim.
Six paths PASS · wardrobe open-state comparison PASS · source furniture is not silently replaced.
Why this matters: relocating the en suite must leave a coherent third bedroom; an empty former bathroom is not a furnished-room result.
This candidate chooses ordinary one-sided double-bed access. It does not invent a household preference or claim two usable bedside routes.
Before adoption: coordinate gallery, former wet services, real doors/window actions, current-house identities and all affected downstream studies.
